title: My first code review
text:
Last week I opened my first pull request at my new job. It was a small change: a new endpoint that returns a list of orders. I was proud of it, so I sent the link to the team and waited.

An hour later, Marta left a comment. She asked me to rename a variable, because "data" says nothing. Then she pointed out that I forgot to handle an empty list. I felt a bit embarrassed, but her tone was friendly. She even added a small tip about how to write a better test.

At first I wanted to defend my code. Then I read the comments again and understood that she was right. I fixed everything in twenty minutes and pushed the changes.

In the evening, the pull request was approved. My lead told me that nobody writes perfect code, and a review is not an exam. It is just another pair of eyes. Now I try to review other people's code the same way: I always say one good thing before I ask for a change.

questions.prompt: How did the reviewer, Marta, behave?
options: She was rude and refused to help.
She gave useful comments in a friendly way.
She rewrote all the code herself.
questions.explanation: Марта залишила корисні коментарі та дала пораду щодо тесту, і її тон був дружнім.

questions.prompt: What did the author understand after reading the comments again?
options: A review is a kind of exam.
questions.explanation: Спочатку автор хотів захищати код, але потім зрозумів, що Марта має рацію.

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the text?
options: A review is a chance to improve, not a test.
Pull requests should never be small.
Leads must write all the tests.
questions.explanation: Лід каже, що рев'ю - це не іспит, а ще одна пара очей.
